Office of the Supreme People's Court

Notice on Serving Judicial Documents in Foreign-Related Administrative Cases to Foreign Countries

Fa Ban [2004] No. 346

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Since China's accession to the World Trade Organization, the number of foreign-related administrative cases heard by Chinese courts has been increasing. To protect the lawful rights and interests of Chinese and foreign parties and to ensure the smooth progress of trial work in Chinese courts, reference may now be made to the Hague Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters, to which China has acceded, to request foreign assistance in serving judicial documents in China's foreign-related administrative cases. The following is hereby notified regarding the practice of serving judicial documents in foreign-related administrative cases to foreign countries:

For cases where judicial documents in foreign-related administrative cases need to be served in a member state of the Hague Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters, reference may be made to the Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters, concluded at The Hague in 1965, and the relevant domestic procedures of China, to submit a request for judicial assistance to the relevant foreign country and effect service through the channels provided by the Convention.

July 20, 2004
